audit.reasoning: The coding (fixed-dominant, final: 01 001 0001, dom=true, strict=false) rests on the language's only phonology, Regnier 1993, written by the resident field linguist, with an explicit stress section. The PDF was not held before; I fetched sources it from the cited Wayback URL and confirmed the quotation verbatim at p. 39 fn. 3 and p. 51 sec. 5.1. The text supports exactly the catalog's reading: final stress in polysyllables with one lexical exception (possibly monosyllabic/onomatopoeic), most words monosyllabic, most disyllables compounds or Spanish loans. No later or instrumental description of Quiegolani stress was found in Glottolog or on the web; Black's 1994/2000 syntax works are the only larger descriptions and are print-only, so they are low-priority wishlist items that are unlikely to change the coding. sources.citation: Regnier 1993, Quiegolani Zapotec phonology, SIL-UND Work Papers 37, secs. fn.3 and 5.1 (PDF via web.archive.org snapshot 20240724070649 of commons.und.edu viewcontent article=1323)
sources.quote: Most QZ words are monosyllabic. In polysyllabic words stress almost always occurs on the last syllable. ... When two-syllable words occur, the stress is on the second syllable, as in ca'Yet 'basket'. The exception to this rule is the word 'nwjider 'acorn woodpecker', where stress falls on the first syllable.

sources.quote: p.39 fn.3: 'Most QZ words are monosyllabic. In polysyllabic words stress almost always occurs on the last syllable. Stress is marked on polysyllabic words.' p.51 §5.1: 'The vast majority of QZ morphemes are monosyllabic. Most of the two-syllable words we have recorded are known to be either compounds or Spanish loanwords... When two-syllable words occur, the stress is on the second syllable, as in ca4'Yet2 'basket'. The exception to this rule is the word 'nwžider 'acorn woodpecker', where stress falls on the first syllable.' Also p.59-60: Spanish loans typically retain only the stressed syllab
